feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: In `blocker_moved`, the scan clause `for front in [env.grid.get(x - 1, y)]` evaluates the front-cell lookup for every scanned (x, y) cell, including x == 0, so it calls env.grid.get with coordinate -1 — outside the documented grid range 0 <= x < env.width. The `x > 0` test only sits later in the boolean chain and cannot prevent this lookup, because the `for front` clause runs unconditionally before the boolean expression is evaluated. Necessary fix: make sure the (x-1, y) lookup is only evaluated after the scanned cell is known to be a door with x > 0 — i.e., compute and read the front cell inside the short-circuit chain following the door-type and x > 0 checks (or otherwise filter the scanned cells before binding `front`), so no out-of-range coordinate is ever passed to env.grid.get. Everything else is fine: `has_door_key` correctly expresses carrying a key matching the door's color with properly guarded attribute reads, the predicate set covers exactly the declared propositions, and `blocker_moved`'s ball logic itself matches the specification (true when the start-side cell in front of the door holds no ball, including while the ball is carried, and false again if it is dropped back there) once the lookup guard is added.

NO CHANGES NEEDED. The candidate covers exactly the declared propositions {blocker_moved, has_door_key}, one predicate each, correct names, each taking exactly `env`. Both are persistent conditions and read only the current observation; neither touches RM state, descriptions, rewards, or episode_memory, which is correct since no event propositions are declared. `blocker_moved` scans the grid for the door, guards `cell is not None` before reading `cell.type`, guards the adjacent cell with `front is None` before reading `front.type`, and reports true exactly when the start-side cell in front of the door (x-1, matching the documented left-start/right-target layout) is empty or holds a non-ball object; this matches the table semantics 'the cell in front of the door holds no ball', turns true on the ball's pickup, and turns false again if the ball is dropped back there. With the single locked door the environment guarantees, the `any` over doors reduces to the unique door's check. `has_door_key` guards `env.carrying is not None` before reading its attributes and requires the carried key's color to match the door's color, matching 'the agent carries a key whose color equals the door's color'. Only allowed builtins (`any`, `range`) and documented API surface (`env.grid.get`, `env.width`, `env.height`, `env.carrying`, `type`/`color`) are used, including the sanctioned list-binding scan idiom; bodies are single expression returns with no assignments, loops, imports, or sibling calls.
